stem:
Chloramine, $\text{NH}_2\text{Cl}$, can be used in the treatment of drinking water to kill bacteria. Excess chloramine is destroyed using UV light. The mechanism for this involves free radicals. $$\text{NH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} \bullet\text{NH}_2 + \bullet\text{Cl}$$

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
What is meant by the term *free radical*?

The equation for a possible propagation step in the process is shown.

$$\text{NH}_2\text{Cl} + \bullet\text{Cl} \rightarrow \bullet\text{NHCl} + \text{HCl}$$

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest an equation for a possible termination step in this process.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram for $\text{NH}_2\text{Cl}$. Show outer electrons only.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the hybridisation of the nitrogen atom and suggest the $\text{H-N-Cl}$ bond angle in the $\text{NH}_2\text{Cl}$ molecule.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Standard enthalpies of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}$, and standard entropies, $S^{\ominus}$, are shown in the table.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Define the meaning of the term entropy.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.stem: Hydrazine, $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$, can be produced from chloramine and ammonia as shown. $$\text{NH}_2\text{Cl(g)} + \text{NH}_3\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{H}_4\text{(g)} + \text{HCl(g)}$$
parts.text: Calculate the standard entropy change, $\Delta S^{\ominus}$, for this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the standard enthalpy change, $\Delta H^{\ominus}$, for this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Calculate the standard Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G^{\ominus}$, for this reaction at 298 K.

parts.label: (c)(v)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to $\Delta G^{\ominus}$, why this reaction becomes less feasible at higher temperatures.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Compare and explain the basicities of ammonia, ethylamine and phenylamine.
